scores.evidence: Every screen has a visual anchor: the hook-predict cards, step lists with expected results, prompt blocks with highlighted fields, the practice-flow diagram and the practice-checklist. The practice-flow diagram (flowchart TD, 4 nodes) reads well at 390 px in pages/mobile-jp-11.png, and its labels are Japanese in JP and English in EN.

There are no walls of text and textOnlyScreens is empty in all three runs. Desktop JP has a median of 36 chars/line (target 30–40) but a maximum of 44, and EN has a median of 70 (target 60–75) but a maximum of 80. The longest lines are the wide prompt and checklist rows. The four sequential question screens in check-quiz (mobile-jp-14..16) are long but are broken up into separate cards.

The EN screenshots have no untranslated Japanese, and the JP screenshots have no stray English beyond the intended MoSCoW terms. Text contrast and focus targets look adequate, and no controls are hidden under the 56/60 px top and bottom bars on mobile. Metrics show overflowX false, 0 console errors, 0 mermaid errors, 0 unknown blocks and 0 broken images.

niceToHave: reader: on mobile the flashcard hint says 「クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる」 (pages/mobile-jp-18.png). On touch devices it should say tap (タップでめくる).

reader: the end banner 「このコースの最後のレッスンまで読み終えました」 appears for a chapter 2 draft (pages/mobile-jp-19.png, desktop-jp-13.png). This is probably because drafts are not listed in course.json. Consider wording that is specific to preview mode.

reader: on mobile, Japanese line breaks fall inside words in prompt bodies, for example 「質問を1つず／つ」 in practice-prompt-interview (pages/mobile-jp-05.png) and 「どうな／れる」 in practice-prompt-plan (pages/mobile-jp-10.png). Phrase-aware breaking (word-break: auto-phrase or BudouX) would fix this.

practice-flow: on desktop the vertical 4-node diagram leaves a lot of empty width (pages/desktop-jp-07.png, desktop-jp-08.png). This is acceptable because TD is the right choice for mobile. Leave it as is unless the reader supports a separate desktop direction.
summary: The page is clean on mobile JP, desktop JP and desktop EN. Nothing overflows, nothing is clipped, every screen has a visual anchor and both locales are fully localized. The remaining issues are minor reader-level details: the flashcard hint wording on touch screens, the end-of-course banner on a draft and Japanese line breaks inside words. None of them require a change to the lesson content.
